result: Malaria caused 429,000 deaths worldwide in 2016, with approximately 70% being African children under 5 years of age.
evaluation: Claim C1 cites the WHO Malaria Report 2016 as the source for these mortality statistics. This is a well-established and authoritative source for global malaria burden data, making this background claim well-supported.

result: Orange vessels and severe foveal whitening on clinical examination are strongly associated with death in children with P. falciparum cerebral malaria, with associations remaining significant after adjusting for confounders.
evaluation: Claims C2 and C3 report unadjusted associations from 817 subjects with statistically significant odds ratios and appropriate confidence intervals. Claims C23 and C24 demonstrate that these associations persist in multivariable regression after controlling for age, WCC, HRP2, lactate, and papilloedema, though with reduced sample sizes (n=549 and n=615). The statistical methods appear appropriate and the effect sizes are clinically meaningful.

result: Arteriolar involvement by intravascular filling defects on fluorescein angiography is associated with death and longer recovery times, with large arteriole sequestration conferring a 2.81-fold increased risk of death.
evaluation: Claims C4, C66, and C85 consistently report that large arteriole sequestration is significantly associated with death (OR 2.81, p<0.02) from the FA dataset of 260 subjects. Claims C68-C70 and C84 show associations with longer recovery times using binomial regression. The precapillary arteriole association with death (C67, OR 2.47, p=0.065) approaches but does not reach significance. The interpretation (C86) that arteriolar involvement indicates greater sequestration load is reasonable given the data.

result: Orange vessels contain dense sequestration of late-stage parasitized red blood cells involving 360° of the lumen circumference, with high sensitivity (0.97) and specificity (0.89) for this extent of sequestration.
evaluation: Claims C5-C6 and C25 describe the histopathological findings from 29 cases showing pRBCs sequestered around the vessel circumference. Claims C28-C32 provide diagnostic test accuracy statistics from analysis of 412 vessels from 9 cases, showing excellent sensitivity (0.97) and good specificity (0.89) with appropriate confidence intervals. The conclusion (C74, C78) that orange vessels indicate severe sequestration is well-supported by the clinicopathological correlation.

result: White vessels contain primarily extraerythrocytic haemozoin and are associated with capillary non-perfusion but not with death.
evaluation: Claim C26 describes the histopathological composition of white vessels. Claims C80-C81 interpret that white capillaries are not associated with death and correlate with non-perfusion on FA. This is supported by the lack of association between white capillaries and death in Table 1 (OR 0.75, p=0.17) and the FA correlation data.

result: Intraretinal sequestration is associated with significantly reduced expression of CD34, SMA, and PDGFRβ in retinal microvessels, indicating severe dysfunction or loss of pericytes and endothelial cells.
evaluation: Claims C33-C35 report statistically significant associations (all p<0.005) between sequestration and reduced expression of vascular markers. Claims C36-C41 provide quantitative data showing dramatic reductions in continuous immunostaining in vessels with sequestration compared to those without (e.g., CD34: 14±9% vs 90±10%). Claim C43 links reduced PDGFRβ to hemorrhages. The interpretation (C42, C76, C87) that this indicates pericyte/endothelial dysfunction is reasonable based on established knowledge of these markers.

result: Glial cells surrounding vessels with severe sequestration show increased expression of ICAM-1 and GFAP, markers of early and late glial activation, with effects likely including blood-retinal barrier breakdown.
evaluation: Claims C44-C45 report statistically significant increases in ICAM-1 (p=0.003) and GFAP (p=0.034) in 10 of 21 MR-positive cases. Claims C46-C47 cite appropriate references for the temporal characteristics of these markers. Claim C48 provides negative control data. Claim C49 shows association with discolored vessels (p<0.05). The interpretation (C92) about BRB/BBB breakdown is an inference supported by the data and cited literature, though direct evidence of barrier breakdown is not provided.

result: Retinal whitening is topographically associated with tissue hypoxia, as evidenced by increased VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression in inner retinal layers, with correlations to whitening severity.
evaluation: Claims C51-C54 show VEGFR1 expression is increased in MR-positive cases and positively correlated with whitening severity (p<0.05, p<0.001). Claims C55-C58 demonstrate similar findings for AQP4 with densitometry analysis (p<0.05). Claims C59-C60 report co-localization of thrombi with whitening. The interpretation (C77, C96) that this indicates inner retinal ischemia is supported by the localization data and established knowledge of VEGFR1 (C94) and AQP4 (C95) function. Claim C93 cites prior work establishing the topographical association.

result: Intravascular filling defects occur very frequently in venules (80-98% of vessels) but are much less common in arterioles (15-58%), with no association between post-capillary venule sequestration and survival.
evaluation: Claims C62-C64 and C82-C83 report frequencies of IVFD from the FA dataset of 260 subjects, showing very high rates in venules and lower rates in arterioles. Claim C65 reports no significant association between post-capillary venule sequestration and survival (OR 0.23, p=0.053), which approaches but does not reach significance. The data are clearly presented and the statistical analysis appears appropriate.

result: Papilloedema and disc hyperaemia, both indicators of brain swelling, are more likely in children who died.
evaluation: Claims C20-C21 report statistically significant associations from Table 1 with appropriate odds ratios and confidence intervals (papilloedema: OR 2.29, p<0.001; disc hyperaemia: OR 1.73, p<0.01). Claim C22 correctly identifies these as indicators of brain swelling based on established medical knowledge. The sample size (n=817) is adequate.

result: Subjects without admission retinal examination had higher serum lactate, were more likely to die, and were younger and lighter than those examined.
evaluation: Claims C14-C17 report statistically significant differences between examined and non-examined subjects with appropriate p-values. This analysis addresses potential selection bias in the study. The statistical comparisons appear appropriate and the differences are clearly documented.

result: Of 817 subjects with retinopathy-positive CM, 137 (16.8%) died, with the majority dying within 24 hours of admission.
evaluation: Claims C18-C19 report basic descriptive statistics from the clinical dataset. The mortality rate and temporal data are clearly stated and consistent with the study design.

result: Between 2009 and 2014, 260 subjects underwent fluorescein angiography, though capillary sequestration was ungradeable in 62% of cases.
evaluation: Claim C61 describes the FA dataset size and timeframe. Claim C71 acknowledges a methodological limitation regarding capillary grading. This is an honest reporting of study limitations.

result: Automated image analysis showed higher ratios of affected vessels in children who died (41.9% vs 37.8%), but this difference did not reach statistical significance.
evaluation: Claims C72-C73 report results from automated vessel segmentation analysis of 251 eyes. The trend toward higher IVFD in deaths is noted but appropriately reported as non-significant (OR 18.05, p<0.08). The very wide confidence interval (0.74-211.33) suggests high uncertainty, possibly due to small numbers of deaths (n=33) or methodological issues with the automated analysis.

result: Fibrin polymers were detected in retinal capillaries and venules.
evaluation: Claim C27 reports detection of fibrin polymers using fibrinogen immunohistochemistry, with supporting figure reference. This is a straightforward histopathological observation.

result: Background claims about cerebral malaria pathophysiology and malarial retinopathy features are established in the literature.
evaluation: Claims C10-C13 cite appropriate references for established knowledge about CM pathophysiology (Turner, 1997), retinal examination methods (Harding et al., 2006), MR features, and prognostic associations (Beare et al., 2004; Lewallen et al., 2008; Beare et al., 2006). These are well-supported background claims.

result: Visible sequestration is strongly associated with death, with increased risk when arterioles are involved.
evaluation: Claim C75 is a summary statement integrating findings from both the clinical dataset (n=817) and FA dataset (n=260). This is well-supported by the individual claims about orange vessels (C2, C23) and arteriolar involvement (C4, C66).

result: Orange vessels can be detected clinically with indirect ophthalmoscopy after pupil dilation, though expertise is mainly available in research or tertiary centers.
evaluation: Claims C79 and C97 describe the clinical detection method and cite appropriate references (Taylor et al., 2004; Swamy et al., 2018) regarding availability of expertise. This is supported by the study's own methodology and cited literature.

result: Pericytes are highly sensitive to hypoxia, and retina and brain may have similar pericyte dysfunction/loss in fatal pediatric CM.
evaluation: Claims C88-C89 cite appropriate references (Kamouchi et al., 2012; Bergers and Song, 2005) for established knowledge about pericyte biology. Claim C90 cites Greiner et al., 2015 for retina-brain parallels. Claim C91 is an inference based on unpublished brain data showing similar pericyte changes, which is appropriately presented as suggestive rather than definitive.

result: Clinicopathological features of CM in the retina parallel those in the brain, and including children without MR in clinical trials may reduce power to detect intervention effects.
evaluation: Claim C98 cites multiple studies (Barrera et al., 2015; MacCormick et al., 2014; White et al., 2009; Dorovini-Zis et al., 2011) supporting retina-brain parallels. Claim C99 is a reasonable inference based on MR increasing diagnostic specificity for CM, though it is presented as a recommendation rather than empirical finding.
